newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds were weaker in late trade, coming under pressure before the Swiss federal government's announcement of a new bond tender on Tuesday.
Traders were waiting for the conditions and the size of the offering, which may be for one or more tranches.

Some traders have expected a reopening of existing issues. The most likely candidates were seen as the 4-1/2 percent June 2007 bond CH470458= or the 4-1/4 percent January CH108546= 2008 as likely choices for a reopening.
But one trader saw a possibility that the Swiss government would launch an entirely new, 12-year issue.

"One could bring the 2007 or the 2008. Or, what I would expect, is that they would bring a 2009 4-1/4 percent with maybe a yield of 4.12 to 4.15 percent. I think that would be very interesting," the trader said.
Of the two outstanding issues in question, he believed that the 4-1/4 percent 2007 bond was more likely to be reopened, because it has less outstanding volume than the 2008 bond.
The yield spread between Swiss and German cash bonds meanwhile continued to narrow, and was at 185 to 186 basis points during the afternoon YLDS3, from levels over 200 seen recently.
The spread is still wider however than the roughly 140 basis points seen in the spring.

Christian Heyden, analyst at CS Research, said that the spread has tended to narrow recently as German bonds gained in attractiveness relative to the Swiss market. But he saw Swiss yields also maintaining current levels or moving slightly lower.
Dec Conf futures CONFZ6 down 10 at 114.95.
Dec Comi medium-term bond COMIZ6 up 10 at 109.90
Dec Euro Swiss francs FESM6 down one at 97.74.
